parallel.requirements: Recognized the full Flasky target: app factory, auth, main, API blueprints, models, templates/static files, migrations, dependencies, package metadata, and official pytest acceptance.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned the core implementation and integration, delegated only top-level boilerplate to one child, then launched a broad nine-agent verification workflow for official suites, spec probes, robustness, packaging, and verifiers.
parallel.implementation: Built a complete Flask app with user roles, posts, comments, follows, REST API, template surface, deployment files, test compatibility shims, role auto-seeding, migrations, and package metadata.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the boilerplate child's shared-workspace outputs and kept implementation work in the parent; artifact validation captured a complete workspace, but the agent did not produce a final message before process timeout.
parallel.verification: Ran local smoke tests, migration checks, route/API probes, import checks, and launched verifier children; several children returned successful reports and one low packaging issue, but the workflow aggregate never returned.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation passed 34 of 34, but process_ok was false, the final response was empty, and the verifier workflow was killed with some probe work still in progress.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Flasky task requirements and worked from the provided specification without delegation or subagents.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single parent actor owned discovery, implementation, tests, packaging, cleanup, and final reporting in a sequential plan.
serial.implementation: Created the full app package, models, auth/main/API blueprints, templates, static assets, migrations, dependency pins, setup.py, README, deployment files, and tests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All files were written directly by the serial parent into one workspace; it cleaned transient files and delivered a final textual summary.
serial.verification: Ran pytest suites, Flask CLI tests, migration/deploy checks, route and API smoke checks, fake-data probes, install checks, and public API import checks before ending.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official failure is present; the serial process completed normally with 34 of 34 official tests passing and a final report noting no submit tool.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the complete Flasky application requirements and built the required project surface.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt requirements and built the same functional surface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage difference affected the official outcome; both current evaluations passed all 34 tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split top-level boilerplate to one child and verification to a wide workflow while the parent retained implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no delegation and the single parent owned the entire implementation, verification, and final report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The major difference is parallel's extra verification fan-out; serial kept ownership centralized and finished without subagent lifecycle work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel briefs gave children focused scopes: boilerplate avoided app code, and verifier children received a shared spec facts block and read-only workspace rules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent handoffs or interface briefs because all context remained with one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No interface mismatch caused a solution difference; the parallel context boundary that mattered was the verifier workflow result lifecycle rather than missing task context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote the Flasky modules, fixed compatibility gaps, hardened token handling, and verified examples while background agents probed the same app.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the project sequentially, added tests, fixed the same Flask 0.12 JSON client and role-seeding issues, and continued through packaging and cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The produced application behavior converged; parallel overlapped verification with late fixes while serial performed comparable fixes in a single linear trace.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received several child and verifier results, but the workflow aggregate stayed null and killed before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial local test results were immediately available to the same actor and were incorporated into the final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the aggregate verifier return due the still-running workflow; serial had no inter-agent result lifecycle to join.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel allowed a boilerplate child to write top-level files in the shared workspace, but the child reported no app Python files touched and the parent integrated the resulting tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all project files itself and cleaned generated caches before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete write collision or contamination is evidenced; shared writing was present only for top-level boilerplate and did not corrupt the passing artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran multiple smoke and adversarial checks and the current official evaluator passed the final artifact, but its verifier workflow did not reach a final aggregate.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local pytest, Flask CLI, migration, route, API, and import checks, then the current official evaluator passed the final artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both achieved official acceptance; serial's verification closed cleanly while parallel's expanded verifier workflow remained incomplete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full agent budget, was terminated with returncode 143, and left the final response empty after exit 137 during probe-suite replay.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished with returncode 0, retained about 85 seconds of budget, and wrote a final completion summary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete closure difference is process completion: serial closed normally, while parallel timed out because verifier fan-out and replay occupied the end of the run.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in the current completed evaluations: both artifacts passed 34 of 34 official tests. The task-solving difference is procedural, not score-based. Parallel produced a passing workspace but timed out while an overbroad verifier workflow remained killed and unaggregated; serial produced a passing workspace and a normal final report after sequential verification.
parallel_contributors: Passing implementation of the Flasky routes, models, API, templates, migrations, and packaging files.
Broad parallel verification produced useful partial evidence but consumed closure time and left no aggregate workflow result.
serial_contributors: Passing implementation of the same Flasky functional surface.
Sequential local testing and cleanup completed before a final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: No ordinary coding defect explains an outcome gap because there is no outcome gap.
The packaging sdist issue surfaced by the parallel verifier was low-severity and outside the official tests; it did not affect the official pass.
evaluator_effects: The evaluator scores the saved workspace artifact, so the parallel process timeout and empty final response did not prevent solution_passed from being true.

candidates.reason: The parent implemented the app modules directly; delegation did not leave required implementation without an owner.
The parent kept integration ownership and reconciled the shared workspace; no incompatible independently owned components required unassigned integration.
The final workspace artifact was assembled and validated; top-level files and app files were present despite process timeout.
The parent maintained the implementation, verification, and delivery pipeline; the problem was budget exhaustion in verification fan-out, not absent pipeline ownership.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory preflight; the parent wrote and tested the app before and during verification.
The run did not perform investigation as a separate first phase before productive work; implementation preceded and overlapped verifier activity.
No indispensable implementation path was starved of workers; the artifact was complete and passed, while the direct adverse chain was excessive verifier breadth.

The parent launched a nine-agent verifier workflow late in the run, observed only six results, then spent the remaining window replaying generated suites and was killed before workflow aggregation or a final response.
candidates.realized_consequence: The verifier workflow and parent-side replay consumed the closure window, leaving a killed workflow with result null, an interrupted test replay, and no final response despite an officially passing artifact.
candidates.near_match_reason: A verifier result was trapped below the workflow, but the aggregate result was absent because the broad verifier fan-out exhausted the deadline; taxonomy precedence assigns that chain to Fan-out Budget Exhaustion.

candidates.reason: The adverse budget episode came from collective verifier breadth, not one demonstrably overbroad child whose own required deliverable was the bottleneck.
The boilerplate and verifier children received concrete scopes and relevant constraints; no missing known requirement in a child brief made work unusable.
Separate agents were not assigned interdependent implementation components with omitted contracts; the boilerplate child avoided app code and verifier children were read-only.
No known requirement, finding, or checkpoint is shown disappearing through summary or transfer and causing repeated or wrong work.
The problem was not a too-large returned handoff available to the parent; the workflow never returned an aggregate handoff before closure.
No actor consumed a superseded report or workspace state that caused invalid verification or rework.
Packaging verifier disagreement stayed inside the killed workflow and did not reach the parent as conflicting handoffs requiring adjudication.
The parallel parent did not make a whole-task completion claim before timeout, and it had run substantial integrated checks with the final artifact passing officially.
Verifier follow-up agents received the reported packaging findings to verify; there is no replacement retry that repeated prior work without checkpoint state.

candidates.reason: The workflow was killed at run closure, but this is the terminal symptom of the same fan-out budget episode; no separate parent cancellation of required child work is the governing boundary.
A complete workspace artifact had already been assembled and passed official tests; there was no unpromoted candidate artifact needing late placement.
No implementation child result was merged only after relevant verification without a post-merge check; parent changes were followed by smoke and official evaluation.
The only implementation-like child created boilerplate directly in the shared workspace and reported completion; no retrievable app implementation was left unjoined.
Individual verifier findings were trapped below the workflow, but the missing aggregate return is downstream of the retained broad verifier fan-out exhausting the deadline.
No required implementation child failed and was abandoned; the parent independently continued verification and the artifact passed officially.
Completed child results were not delivered to the parent as an aggregate workflow result at a decision point; this is not an available completed result ignored by the parent.
The parent actively inspected workflow progress and probe scratch directories, then reran test suites; it did not simply wait blindly until timeout.
The boilerplate child wrote documentation and deployment files while the parent owned app code; no competing cross-file behavior or interface design required reconciliation.
No raw evidence shows two live agents editing the same source or configuration file and observing or reconciling a concurrent change.
No agent replaced, deleted, or wholesale rewrote source files produced or actively owned by another agent.
No required executable or submitted entry-point artifact was overwritten while another actor owned or used it.
Cleanup removed transient tests and caches, but there is no broad rebuild or promotion that invalidated another agent's final-tree work.
Multiple actors shared the workspace, but the only child writer had a bounded top-level scope and no concrete unstable-state or provenance failure is shown.
Verifier scratch files and transient caches were noticed but not consumed as stable inputs that contaminated implementation or acceptance.
